{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the increment as extensions to an existing Spring Integration-style module framework rather than modifying the Spring Framework core.",
    "Use Java 17 and the existing project build, dependency-management, module lifecycle, configuration, channel, and partitioning conventions.",
    "Implement WebSocket as an inbound source adapter that converts browser messages and connection events into framework messages, with configurable endpoint and session handling.",
    "Implement AWS source support for Amazon S3 and Amazon SES using the AWS SDK v2 and expose separate configuration options for the supported ingestion modes.",
    "Implement the AWS sink for S3 using configurable bucket, key or prefix, region, credentials, serialization, and write semantics.",
    "Implement the Cassandra sink using the DataStax Java driver and configurable contact points, keyspace, table, consistency, batching, and schema mapping.",
    "Implement the HAWQ sink through the available PXF integration, producing Avro or Parquet according to configuration and using the project's supported HAWQ connectivity mechanism.",
    "Implement the Solr sink using SolrJ or the existing Solr client abstraction, supporting configurable collection, endpoint, document mapping, batching, and commit behavior.",
    "Implement error handling as a framework-level routing mechanism with configurable error channels, exception matching, preservation of the root cause chain, and a hierarchy of global, default, and module-specific exceptions.",
    "Preserve existing partition strategy state and treat dynamic module addition and deletion as compatibility and regression-test concerns rather than redesigning the partitioning subsystem.",
    "Use unit tests with mocks for external services and containerized or integration-environment tests where practical; avoid requiring live AWS, HAWQ, Cassandra, Solr, or browser infrastructure for the normal build.",
    "Provide backward-compatible configuration defaults and fail-fast validation for missing or incompatible module-specific settings."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is added to an existing Java/Spring Integration codebase with established module interfaces, message abstractions, configuration conventions, build automation, and CI.",
    "The existing codebase already includes the GA partition strategy implementation referenced by U8; only regression and dynamic-adaptation testing is required for that story.",
    "The scope includes production-quality implementation, unit tests, integration tests, configuration examples, and developer documentation, but not deployment automation or production operations.",
    "The WebSocket source supports standard WebSocket connections and message ingestion; advanced protocol features, clustering, guaranteed delivery, and browser SDK development are out of scope.",
    "AWS source support is limited to the S3 and SES ingestion use cases explicitly named in U2; support for every AWS service is out of scope.",
    "AWS credentials, regions, retry policies, and endpoint overrides follow standard AWS SDK configuration mechanisms and existing application conventions.",
    "Cassandra, Solr, and HAWQ server installations are not developed as part of this increment; their standard client protocols and compatible test environments are available.",
    "HAWQ PXF accepts the selected Avro or Parquet output path and does not require development of a new PXF connector or HAWQ server-side extension.",
    "The error channel is implemented within the existing message-channel and exception-routing architecture, including custom-module failures, rather than replacing the entire error-handling subsystem.",
    "The estimate represents one experienced developer performing analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and code-quality work; review and release approval by others are not counted as developer effort.",
    "Effort is estimated in workdays, with one workday representing approximately eight hours of productive engineering effort."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and architecture design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing module SPI, configuration model, message and channel abstractions, lifecycle behavior, partitioning implementation, and referenced Spring Integration patterns. Define interfaces, configuration contracts, error semantics, dependency boundaries, and acceptance criteria for all eight stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Build and module scaffolding",
      "activity_description": "Create or update module projects, dependency declarations, Java 17 settings, configuration metadata, test fixtures, logging conventions, and CI build entries for the new source and sink modules.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "WebSocket source module",
      "activity_description": "Implement the WebSocket inbound source, connection and session handling, message conversion, endpoint configuration, lifecycle management, validation, error propagation, and focused unit tests based on the existing Spring Integration WebSocket patterns.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "AWS source module",
      "activity_description": "Implement AWS ingestion for S3 and SES, including client configuration, polling or event-consumption behavior supported by the platform, payload conversion, acknowledgment and retry behavior, credential handling, validation, mocks, and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Cassandra sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement Cassandra connection and session management, configurable keyspace and table mapping, data conversion, batching and consistency options, write-result and failure handling, lifecycle cleanup, and unit tests using mocked driver behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "AWS S3 sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement S3 output, object naming and prefix handling, payload serialization, metadata configuration, client lifecycle, retry and failure behavior, validation, and unit tests with mocked AWS clients.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "HAWQ sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement HAWQ output through the supported PXF path, including Avro and Parquet serialization, destination and connection configuration, batching or file-boundary handling, resource cleanup, failure reporting, and unit tests for both formats.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Solr sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement Solr client integration, collection and endpoint configuration, document mapping, batch submission, commit behavior, retries and failure handling, lifecycle management, and unit tests using a mocked or embedded-compatible Solr client.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Configurable error-channel and exception routing",
      "activity_description": "Implement explicit error-channel configuration, exception matching such as catch-all handling, traversal and preservation of the root cause chain, error payload creation, routing from source, processor, sink, and custom-module failures, and GlobalException, DefaultException, and ModuleSpecificException behavior. Add unit tests for routing precedence and continuation of ingestion.",
      "most_likely_effort": 18
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Partition strategy preservation regression tests",
      "activity_description": "Add tests proving that partition strategy state survives module addition and deletion and that dynamically adapted modules continue to use the correct strategy, including representative source, processor, and sink combinations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Cross-module integration and compatibility testing",
      "activity_description": "Build end-to-end test scenarios connecting sources, processors, sinks, and error channels; test configuration loading, lifecycle transitions, retries, malformed payloads, external-service failures, custom modules, and compatibility with existing modules. Use mocks and containerized services where feasible.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Documentation and configuration examples",
      "activity_description": "Document module configuration, required dependencies, credentials, endpoint and schema options, WebSocket usage, AWS S3 and SES examples, Cassandra, HAWQ, and Solr examples, error-channel configuration, troubleshooting, and limitations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Quality hardening and release preparation",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and test suite, resolve defects, perform static analysis and dependency checks, improve logging and validation, verify packaging and generated metadata, and prepare the increment for release.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 136
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as extensions to an existing Spring Integration-style module framework rather than modifying the Spring Framework core.
Use Java 17 and the existing project build, dependency-management, module lifecycle, configuration, channel, and partitioning conventions.
Implement WebSocket as an inbound source adapter that converts browser messages and connection events into framework messages, with configurable endpoint and session handling.
Implement AWS source support for Amazon S3 and Amazon SES using the AWS SDK v2 and expose separate configuration options for the supported ingestion modes.
Implement the AWS sink for S3 using configurable bucket, key or prefix, region, credentials, serialization, and write semantics.
Implement the Cassandra sink using the DataStax Java driver and configurable contact points, keyspace, table, consistency, batching, and schema mapping.
Implement the HAWQ sink through the available PXF integration, producing Avro or Parquet according to configuration and using the project's supported HAWQ connectivity mechanism.
Implement the Solr sink using SolrJ or the existing Solr client abstraction, supporting configurable collection, endpoint, document mapping, batching, and commit behavior.

Implement error handling as a framework-level routing mechanism with configurable error channels, exception matching, preservation of the root cause chain, and a hierarchy of global, default, and module-specific exceptions.
Preserve existing partition strategy state and treat dynamic module addition and deletion as compatibility and regression-test concerns rather than redesigning the partitioning subsystem.

Use unit tests with mocks for external services and containerized or integration-environment tests where practical; avoid requiring live AWS, HAWQ, Cassandra, Solr, or browser infrastructure for the normal build.
Provide backward-compatible configuration defaults and fail-fast validation for missing or incompatible module-specific settings.
assumptions: The increment is added to an existing Java/Spring Integration codebase with established module interfaces, message abstractions, configuration conventions, build automation, and CI.
The existing codebase already includes the GA partition strategy implementation referenced by U8; only regression and dynamic-adaptation testing is required for that story.
The scope includes production-quality implementation, unit tests, integration tests, configuration examples, and developer documentation, but not deployment automation or production operations.
The WebSocket source supports standard WebSocket connections and message ingestion; advanced protocol features, clustering, guaranteed delivery, and browser SDK development are out of scope.
AWS source support is limited to the S3 and SES ingestion use cases explicitly named in U2; support for every AWS service is out of scope.
AWS credentials, regions, retry policies, and endpoint overrides follow standard AWS SDK configuration mechanisms and existing application conventions.
Cassandra, Solr, and HAWQ server installations are not developed as part of this increment; their standard client protocols and compatible test environments are available.
HAWQ PXF accepts the selected Avro or Parquet output path and does not require development of a new PXF connector or HAWQ server-side extension.
The error channel is implemented within the existing message-channel and exception-routing architecture, including custom-module failures, rather than replacing the entire error-handling subsystem.

The estimate represents one experienced developer performing analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and code-quality work; review and release approval by others are not counted as developer effort.
Effort is estimated in workdays, with one workday representing approximately eight hours of productive engineering effort.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module SPI, configuration model, message and channel abstractions, lifecycle behavior, partitioning implementation, and referenced Spring Integration patterns. Define interfaces, configuration contracts, error semantics, dependency boundaries, and acceptance criteria for all eight stories.
Create or update module projects, dependency declarations, Java 17 settings, configuration metadata, test fixtures, logging conventions, and CI build entries for the new source and sink modules.

Implement the WebSocket inbound source, connection and session handling, message conversion, endpoint configuration, lifecycle management, validation, error propagation, and focused unit tests based on the existing Spring Integration WebSocket patterns.

Implement AWS ingestion for S3 and SES, including client configuration, polling or event-consumption behavior supported by the platform, payload conversion, acknowledgment and retry behavior, credential handling, validation, mocks, and unit tests.

Implement Cassandra connection and session management, configurable keyspace and table mapping, data conversion, batching and consistency options, write-result and failure handling, lifecycle cleanup, and unit tests using mocked driver behavior.

Implement S3 output, object naming and prefix handling, payload serialization, metadata configuration, client lifecycle, retry and failure behavior, validation, and unit tests with mocked AWS clients.

Implement HAWQ output through the supported PXF path, including Avro and Parquet serialization, destination and connection configuration, batching or file-boundary handling, resource cleanup, failure reporting, and unit tests for both formats.

Implement Solr client integration, collection and endpoint configuration, document mapping, batch submission, commit behavior, retries and failure handling, lifecycle management, and unit tests using a mocked or embedded-compatible Solr client.

Implement explicit error-channel configuration, exception matching such as catch-all handling, traversal and preservation of the root cause chain, error payload creation, routing from source, processor, sink, and custom-module failures, and GlobalException, DefaultException, and ModuleSpecificException behavior. Add unit tests for routing precedence and continuation of ingestion.

Add tests proving that partition strategy state survives module addition and deletion and that dynamically adapted modules continue to use the correct strategy, including representative source, processor, and sink combinations.

Build end-to-end test scenarios connecting sources, processors, sinks, and error channels; test configuration loading, lifecycle transitions, retries, malformed payloads, external-service failures, custom modules, and compatibility with existing modules. Use mocks and containerized services where feasible.

Document module configuration, required dependencies, credentials, endpoint and schema options, WebSocket usage, AWS S3 and SES examples, Cassandra, HAWQ, and Solr examples, error-channel configuration, troubleshooting, and limitations.

Run the complete build and test suite, resolve defects, perform static analysis and dependency checks, improve logging and validation, verify packaging and generated metadata, and prepare the increment for release.
